ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, ss. 462.31 and 83.02; Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.); Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, including the individual with significant control (ISC) register requirements; Canada Shipping Act, 2001, S.C. 2001, c. 26; provincial Limited Partnership Acts, including the Alberta Limited Partnership Act, British Columbia Limited Partnership Act, and Nova Scotia Limited Partnership Act, as applicable; Global Affairs Canada sanctions regulations under the United Nations Act and the Special Economic Measures Act. There is no federal limited partnership statute; the limited partnership is therefore formed under a provincial statute, and a CBCA corporation is used for the federal general-partner anchor where required.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or national identity document for each ultimate beneficial owner and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or commissioner for oaths in the UBO's country of residence; original issuing government authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the issuing state if the state is a party to the 1961 Apostille Convention; otherwise full consular legalization through the issuing state's embassy or consulate and Global Affairs Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, incumbency, and corporate register extracts for all corporate UBOs and the general partner entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporations Canada or the applicable provincial corporate registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / consular legalization depending on the origin state; registry-issued certified copies are acceptable when issued under the official seal

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter, institution-backed source of wealth and source of funds declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing regulated financial institution and its AML compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of signatures with Hague Apostille / consular legalization if the banking document is a public document under the law of the origin state; otherwise certified notarial copy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified charter-party, bareboat charter agreement, vessel management agreement, or letter of intent evidencing the commercial substance of the ISIC 5222 offshore supply vessel leasing operation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Counterparty lessee, vessel owner, or independent maritime counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille / consular legalization; certified English or French translation must accompany any non-Canadian document

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential and business address for each UBO, general partner, and nominated director or authorized representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, landlord, local government, or notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized true copy with Hague Apostille / consular legalization; non-English or non-French documents must be accompanied by a certified translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screening against Global Affairs Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act designations, UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list for USD-clearing and cross-border exposure, UK and EU sanctions lists where counterparties have nexus to those jurisdictions, and Canada's Criminal Code terrorist entity designations. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) are identified under the FATF framework, including foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, international organization PEPs, and their family members and close associates. Screening is required for all UBOs, general partners, limited partners with a 25% or greater economic interest, directors, authorized representatives, key officers, counterparty lessees, and bareboat charterers. Screening must be completed in English and French and in the original script of the underlying identity documents. Positive hits require senior-management approval, enhanced source-of-funds verification, and suspicious transaction reporting to FINTRAC where applicable. Continuous re-screening is required at least every 90 days or upon any material change in ownership or chartering personnel.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) for federal CBCA names; NUANS name search report through an approved service provider; for the limited partnership component, the applicable provincial registry portal such as the Alberta Corporate Registry, BC Corporate Registry, or Nova Scotia Registry of Joint Stock Companies
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be in English, French, or both; the legal name must be distinctive and not confusingly similar to existing names in Canada. A limited partnership name must include the legal element 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', 'société en commandite', or 's.e.c.' as applicable. Names must use Roman-script characters with permissible French diacritics; foreign-script names, pictograms, and non-Roman characters are not accepted as the registered legal name, but transliterated or translated equivalents may be used as an extra-provincial trade name. Statutory rules require that the name not imply a corporate, crown, government, professional, or charitable status that is not accurate.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: words or expressions implying government or crown sponsorship
words that falsely suggest professional licensing or public authority
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A NUANS-based name reservation is valid for 90 days and is not administratively renewable; if the reservation expires before the articles or registration certificate are filed, a fresh name search and new reservation are required. If the Director under the CBCA or the provincial registrar rejects the proposed name, the applicant receives written reasons. The applicant may then submit a revised name with written consent from the holder of any conflicting name, file a new NUANS report, or make written representations to the competent authority. For federal CBCA name decisions, judicial review may be sought by filing an application in the Federal Court of Canada within the applicable statutory limitation period. For provincial limited partnership name refusals, the appeal and reconsideration procedure of the relevant provincial registry governs.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A CBCA general-partner corporation must maintain a registered office at a physical address in the province of registration; a post-office box or virtual address alone is not sufficient. Provincial limited partnership statutes allow a registered office at the physical office of a licensed registered agent. A virtual office is therefore permissible only if the LP appoints an in-province registered agent with a physical service-of-process address and the arrangement does not misrepresent the entity's operational location. For the ISIC 5222 offshore supply vessel leasing scope, Transport Canada and the Canadian vessel registration regime require the vessel's authorized representative to have a place of business in Canada and a genuine operational presence for maritime documents, inspections, and safety management. A purely virtual office, without a maritime operations office or physical agent, is considered inadequate commercial substance for the vessel chartering model.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 35-45% chance of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months of active chartering. The Canada Revenue Agency may conduct GST/HST or income tax field visits; Transport Canada may perform vessel, operations, and safety inspections under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 with limited or no prior notice; and FINTRAC may conduct an on-site compliance examination of AML records and UBO files. The probability is heightened for offshore marine charter models due to the statutory licence and vessel registry interface.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Partnership Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. P-3, Part 2 (Limited Partnerships) as the formation statute; Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, s. 10 for the corporate general partner; Canada Shipping Act, 2001, S.C. 2001, c. 26 for maritime operational compliance.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) and the Provincial Registrar of Companies (Corporate Registry) of the selected registered-office province.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Limited Partnership (Declaration of Limited Partnership) and Extra-Provincial Registration Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Canadian limited partnership; capital contributions are set by the Partnership Agreement and must be wired into the partnership’s escrow or operating account at formation (no state-mandated escrow deposit).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner hereby adopts the Partnership Agreement and approves the subscription of the initial capital contributions by the limited partners as set forth in Schedule A. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Partnership be established at [Registered Address], Province of [Jurisdiction], and that the Registrar of Companies files the Declaration of Limited Partnership and all ancillary statutory forms. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed as the initial General Partner and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer and Compliance Officer, each authorized to open bank accounts, execute charter and vessel-lease agreements, and effect regulatory filings. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers are authorized to take all actions necessary to obtain the Offshore Supply Vessel operating license and environmental permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada and the provincial Corporate Registry via the NUANS system (ised-isde.canada.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request for a distinct limited partnership name and reserve the name for up to 90 days for a nominal fee; obtain the name reservation report before filing the declaration.
required_dossiers: Authorization letter from the proposed general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or conflicts with a prior registration, select a second draft name or file a written consent-to-use letter from the conflicting holder and re-file the NUANS reservation within the remaining reservation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Partnership Agreement and Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Registrar of Companies (Corporate Registry) of the registered-office province
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Limited Partnership Agreement among the general and limited partners; file the Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form LP-1) with the registrar together with the statutory filing fee, the name reservation report, and the notarized consent of the appointed registered-office provider.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a Notice of Correction, cure the defective field (e.g., partner legal names or address) and re-submit the corrected declaration within 15 days of the notice to avoid administrative rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Extra-Provincial Registration and CRA Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada (ISED) and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership and its corporate general partner extra-provincially with Corporations Canada and obtain a CRA Business Number (BN) with program accounts for GST/HST, payroll, corporate income tax, and import/export where applicable.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation of the corporate general partner
Identification details of all partners (for beneficial ownership registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA denies the BN application for incomplete attestations, correct the attestation form and resubmit with the relevant partnership agreement schedule and partner identification within 30 days of the denial notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Appointment and Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Notice of Registered Office and Notice of General Partner/Officers; establish the statutory records (partner ledger, capital accounts, minutes of partnership meetings) at the registered office and appoint the registered-office provider.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as registered-office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice is rejected for an invalid physical address, amend the notice with a compliant civil address and re-file within 10 days; a post-office box address alone is not acceptable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Capital Contribution Escrow
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Schedule I Canadian chartered bank (e.g., RBC, TD, BMO) or a licensed escrow agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the executed partnership agreement, certificate of registration, and the board resolution to the financial institution; deposit the initial capital contributions into the dedicated escrow or partnership operating account and obtain bank confirmation for the AML/KYC file.
required_dossiers: First board resolution (banking and borrowing authority)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank triggers enhanced due diligence under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, furnish the requested organizational chart, ultimate beneficial owner declarations, and source-of-wealth documentation within 20 business days to avoid account suspension.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Statutory Filings and Tax Elections
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency and the provincial corporate registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the initial annual return with the provincial registry; elect the partnership’s fiscal period for income tax purposes; register the GST/HST account if annual worldwide taxable supplies of the partnership exceed CAD 30,000; and file the CRA partnership information return (T5013) schedule for all partners.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return or T5013 filing deadline is missed, apply for late-filing relief under provincial registry and CRA administrative rules, pay the prescribed late-filing fee, and submit a voluntary disclosure to mitigate penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Transport Canada Marine Safety and Security Directorate
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Offshore Supply Vessel Operating Licence and Ship Safety Certificate (including Station Bill and Flag State Compliance under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) with the Impact Assessment Agency of Canada
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Registration under the Impact Assessment Act (S.C. 2019, c. 28) for routine offshore chartering; Full EIA Report directed only if operations enter Arctic waters, marine protected areas, or significant fish habitat zones.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the Vessel Pollution and Dangerous Chemicals Regulations (SOR/2012-69): oil discharge <15 ppm; no untreated sewage within 3 nm of shore; treated wastewater pH 6.0–9.0; MARPOL Annex VI NOx/SOx emission caps; ballast water exchange standards under SOR/2021-120; and zero discharge of harmful substances within 12 nm of any Canadian coast.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Canadian Coast Guard port state control clearance; Fire Safety Plan review and certification by the provincial Office of the Fire Marshal for any onshore shore-base premises; structural load inspection of crane and A-frame installations; and workplace clearance for crew accommodation and hazardous classified areas under the Canada Occupational Health and Safety Regulations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), operating under the Bank of Canada Act; foreign exchange policy and licensing coordination under the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully flexible exchange rate regime with no capital or current account convertibility restrictions. The Canadian dollar is freely convertible. Profit remittances by non-resident partners of a Canadian limited partnership are permitted without exchange control approval, subject to withholding tax rules under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and applicable income tax treaties. No prior central bank authorization is required for dividend, interest, royalty, or partnership distribution remittances. However, the transaction must be consistent with the partnership's governing agreements and comply with anti-money laundering (AML) reporting thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts in Canada. Offshore vessel charter hire received in foreign currency may be retained, converted at arm's-length market rates, or used directly to settle foreign-currency liabilities. Canadian reporting obligations are limited to tax disclosure and FINTRAC transaction reporting for cross-border wire transfers exceeding CAD 10,000, not to any surrender requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Canadian Dollar Operating Account and USD Foreign Currency Account
Business Operating Account with Maritime Industry Cash Management
Capital Escrow Account for Vessel Lease Security Deposits
USD Clearing Account and Cross-Border Trade Settlement Account
Operational Account with SWIFT and LC Processing
Specialized Escrow Account for Maritime Charter Transactions

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for routine payment collection; Low for full treasury centralization. Offshore digital EMI platforms can be used only as auxiliary collection channels, not as a substitute for a regulated Canadian Schedule I bank account due to the vessel-lease escrow requirement. EMIs must be registered with FINTRAC as money services businesses (MSBs) if serving Canadian clients, and must comply with the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). The limited partnership should maintain its primary liquidity and escrow balances with a Canadian-regulated bank; offshore EMIs may be acceptable only for minor operational disbursements with transaction limits below FINTRAC large-transaction reporting thresholds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of all directors is not strictly mandated for Canadian federal limited partnerships unless the bank's enhanced due diligence policy requires it. Major Canadian banks generally permit remote onboarding via secure video verification and notarized/certified documents, subject to the following conditions: (1) the partnership is validly registered in a province or under the Canada Business Corporations Act (if applicable); (2) ultimate beneficial owners are identified; and (3) document attestation is provided by a Canadian legal counsel or a recognized notary public. For the offshore supply vessel chartering industry, a physical meeting may be required for the general partner or responsible officer when the vessel is flagged outside Canada, or when the partnership is classified as medium-risk enhanced by internal AML policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident general partner or non-resident ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) ownership above 25%
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of passport pages, proof of residential address, source of wealth and source of funds statements, corporate registry extracts, organizational chart, and a legal opinion from Canadian counsel confirming the LP structure and UBO chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Vessel ownership or chartering structure involving a foreign-flagged vessel and offshore holding company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vessel registration certificates (flag state), International Safety Management (ISM) certificates, charter party agreements, commercial invoices, marine insurance policies, and a description of operational rationale for the offshore structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a high-risk jurisdiction or involving cryptocurrency
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statement from the sending institution, proof of underlying commercial transaction (e.g., shareholder loan agreement, charter purchase agreement), tax identification numbers, and a clear source-of-funds narrative supported by notarized affidavits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrow account purpose flagged as potential money laundering or sanctions circumvention
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed escrow agreement, charter hire settlement schedule, vessel bareboat charter or time charter contract, and written confirmation that no sanctioned individuals or entities are counterparties, backed by sanctions screening results.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity and loan capital to the Canadian limited partnership should be routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the investing entity's bank to the partnership's CAD or USD account at a Canadian Schedule I bank. The wire instruction must include a relevant purpose code that accurately describes the transaction, typically corresponding to 'Foreign Direct Investment' (with reference to the OECD Classification of Currency Codes and the bank's internal purpose codes) or 'Intercompany Loan'. Supporting documentation includes the limited partnership agreement, capital contribution schedule, loan note or subscription agreement, and a board or general partner resolution. For amounts exceeding CAD 10,000, FINTRAC reporting applies; for amounts above CAD 100,000, enhanced due diligence and source-of-funds documentation should be pre-positioned. No exchange control approval is required from the Bank of Canada.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlement for vessel fuel, crew wages, port fees, equipment purchases, and charter-hire payments to foreign lessees or sub-charterers should be executed via SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers and irrevocable documentary letters of credit (Commercial LC) for higher-value equipment or fuel supply contracts. For escrow-protected hire collections from charterers, the bank should use a dual-signatory disbursement protocol linked to a maritime escrow agreement. Trade-related disbursements in foreign currency may be paid directly from USD or EUR accounts without mandatory conversion to CAD. All wire transfers must reference a valid underlying invoice or charter party document and remain subject to the bank's sanctions screening and FINTRAC transaction reporting thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward contracts (deliverable) with Canadian Schedule I banks for USD/CAD and EUR/CAD, permitted without exchange control restrictions.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed with a global bank counterparty, generally permissible for hedging less-liquid currency pairs but subject to the Canadian bank's internal credit approval and practical deliverability assessment.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for hedging long-term vessel lease receivables and financing liabilities, permitted under the Canadian Derivatives Rules and subject to the bank's ISDA Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex.

Currency options (puts and calls) on major pairs, permissible for hedging charter hire and vessel acquisition costs; transactions must be embedded in, or supplemental to, a documented underlying commercial exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return with T5013 slips to partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). No federal limited partnership registry exists; this is the principal federal annual filing obligation for the Canadian limited partnership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing due within five months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period; for a calendar-year LP, due by May 31 of the following year, with partner T5013 slips required by the last day of February.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 100 per partner per month, up to CAD 2,500; gross negligence penalties may apply; registry strike-off does not apply to CRA filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Extra-Provincial Limited Partnership Renewal / Annual Declaration of Registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial or territorial registrar under the applicable Limited Partnerships Act where the LP maintains its home or extra-provincial registration (e.g., Alberta Corporate Registry, BC Registrar of Companies, Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the registration anniversary date, or within 30 days after the anniversary, as specified by the provincial LP statute.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-renewal penalties; continued non-renewal for 30 to 90 days triggers administrative deregistration, loss of standing to sue in Canadian courts, and prohibition from carrying on maritime charter activities in the province.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CBCA Annual Return for the Corporate General Partner
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the general partner's incorporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty applies; failure to file for two consecutive years may lead to administrative dissolution of the corporate general partner by Corporations Canada.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T4-T4SUM Return of Compensation Paid (if the LP employs vessel crew or shore staff)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of February following the calendar year in which remuneration was paid.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per slip per day, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 7,500; repeated failure may result in prosecution and administrative sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No federal statutory audit is imposed solely on a Canadian limited partnership. An independent audit becomes mandatory when required by the partnership agreement, financing covenants, a charter or insurance counterparty, or applicable securities law where the LP or the corporate general partner is a reporting issuer. The CRA does not prescribe a monetary audit threshold but may audit partnership records at any time.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) is required for reporting issuers; ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) is available for private enterprises. Financial statements must be prepared on a GAAP-consistent basis and adjusted for Canadian income tax purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For the CBCA corporate general partner, the register of individuals with significant control must be updated within 15 days of any change and reviewed annually at the time the CBCA annual return is prepared. For the LP itself, the annual provincial renewal requires confirmation that any transfer of partnership interests has been recorded in the Register of Partners; no separate federal UBO filing is required for Canadian limited partnerships.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (contribution and transfer history)
Register of Directors of the Corporate General Partner
Minute Book (partnership resolutions and general partner consents)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Pass-through entity: no Canadian federal income tax at the LP level. Partner-level federal CIT: 15% general rate (s. 123(1.1)); 9% Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) small business rate on first CA$500,000; top federal marginal individual rate 33% (plus provincial rates such as Ontario 11.5% general corporate and 20.53% top individual).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Flow-through treatment: income and losses are allocated to partners under the partnership agreement (s. 96 ITA). Federal capital cost allowance (CCA) on support vessels: 15% declining-balance (Class 7) or 25% (Class 41 for offshore drilling units); 50% straight-line for certain Canadian-built vessels under accelerated incentive from Budget 2023 (temporarily includes zero-emission vessels?). Non-tax incentives: Atlas?
